title: The Red Cross and the Gestapo
summary: Briggs says the Red Cross inspections were useless because internees were locked in rooms and the Gestapo accompanied the largely German-Swiss inspectors.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: But, something I want to tell you that I hope the world will understand, one day is that the International Corps for Red Cross doesn't mean a thing.
When they visited our camp, we were closed in our rooms, so what kind of inspection -- how could they inform anyone of what's happening.
They saw no internees at all. We were confined to our rooms, enclosed. Because when they visited, the Gestapo came also to visit with them.
The Gestapo came along with the Red Cross?
Yeh, yeh, with the Red Cross. And the Red Cross, in general, were German-Swiss.

Tough city. I was with Swiss. I mean I worked with Swiss and everything, and I had no trouble with them, but I mean, you're entitled to -- they're Germans, you can say anything you want. They were Germans.
